ratings_why.fun: The curve has a real shape: pips from Tier 1, a wire by Tier 3, the Bean-Counter and Bellringer making long chains pay, and the Rat King as a turn-by-turn capstone; the early turns are still a little quiet.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because Gossip is a stored counter that sets off chains along the zigzag, once per unit per chain, so you build a fuse and choose to spend it now or hold it for the fight; no tribe today plays like that, and the Bad Omen even lights the enemy's fuse.

verdict_why: One real rules gap: how extra uses from the Echo, Bellringer and golden Thirty-Two stack, which sets the golden ceiling.

points.text: Say whether extra uses from the Mill-Chimney Echo, Town-Hall Bellringer and golden Thirty-Two add or multiply. Read plainly they add, but the risks list counts about six uses, which means multiply.
The hold build has no payoff until Hearth Huddle at Tier 5, apart from Old Gundel's rare Blurts. A small Tier 2 or 3 unit that pays for held pips would let you choose hold from the midgame on.
Whisker-Groomer has no Gossip source of its own, so at Tier 2 it often sits idle. A When played: Gossip 1 to the units touching this would keep the early curve moving.
If the Piper's opening burst decides fights, a softer version keeps its feel: Blurting units attack after the next enemy attack instead of at once.

standouts.why: A capstone that turns the whole board into one guaranteed chain each turn, and makes the order of Start of Turn effects a puzzle.
Rewards the length and order of the wire, so placement matters every turn.
Turns the mechanic on the enemy's board; reading their gaps becomes part of play.

weakest.why: A plain buffer that needs others to feed it before it does anything.
Its Gossip only matters in fights and only in the front row; quiet outside the hold build.
No stats and one far pip; useful for crossing gaps, but a low-impact Tier 2.

flags.note: Golden Thirty-Two with a golden Bellringer under the Rat King uses every text many times a turn; stats grow fast, though nothing feeds its own source.
A fully loaded board gets up to seven attacks at Start of Combat before the enemy acts.
With the Rat King, a five-Blurt chain is certain, so this is a free Discover every turn.
How its extra use stacks with the Bellringer's and the golden Thirty-Two's is not stated.
